The portfolio has been built by passionate professionals with decades of experience who seek terroir-oriented wines from around the world.

50 Boutique Wine Importers and Distributors in the USA
29/10/2026 From specialists in natural wines and family estates to regional wholesalers serving independent retailers, these are companies wineries should know when building their U.S. distribution strategy.
For a boutique winery, the right U.S. partner does more than arrange the movement of bottles. It understands the producer, identifies suitable accounts, and gives its sales team a clear reason to recommend the wine.
That makes portfolio fit essential. A specialist in Italian family estates may be well suited to an unfamiliar indigenous variety. A natural-wine importer may place particular importance on farming and cellar practices. A regional distributor may offer the focused market coverage a small winery can realistically support.
The following guide brings together 50 boutique and specialist wine importers and distributors serving the United States. Some are small businesses with tightly focused portfolios; others are larger companies that maintain a strong commitment to independent producers.
Official websites and company portfolio information were checked for this article on October 28, 2026. This is an editorial guide, not a sales ranking. Importing and wholesale distribution are different services, and inclusion does not mean a company is currently accepting new producers.
Importers With a Strong Grower and Estate Focus
1. Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant imports wines from France and Italy, with a portfolio spanning celebrated regions and less familiar appellations. Its producer-centered approach makes it an important reference for wineries studying specialist importing. Producers should examine the existing growers and regional coverage before proposing a fit.
2. Rosenthal Wine Merchant
Rosenthal Wine Merchant emphasizes small, family-owned estates and wines that communicate their origins. Its portfolio includes producers from France, Italy, Switzerland, Spain, and Austria. For wineries, the central question is whether their vineyards, winemaking, and regional identity complement the merchant’s established approach.
3. Louis/Dressner Selections
Louis/Dressner Selections has longstanding relationships with independent growers and a strong interest in farming and winemaking practices. Its website provides extensive producer information and harvest reports. Wineries researching the business should be ready to discuss their work in the vineyard and cellar in detail.
4. Skurnik Wines & Spirits
Skurnik Wines & Spirits combines national importing with direct wholesale distribution in selected states. Its portfolio includes boutique producers from around the world. Suppliers should distinguish between a national import relationship and a proposal for a specific wholesale market, then approach the relevant team accordingly.
5. T. Edward Wines & Spirits
T. Edward Wines & Spirits began with boutique estates and continues to emphasize family-owned producers, craftsmanship, and authenticity. Its business includes importing and distribution. A winery’s introduction should explain the people behind the wine, its production philosophy, and its commercial role within the portfolio.
6. Bowler Wine
Bowler Wine is a New York-based importer and distributor focused on naturally made, small-production wines. Its selection emphasizes personality, regional character, and family growers. Wineries should research both its direct producer relationships and the other import portfolios it represents before making an introduction. NYC Wine Spirits Importer Distributor
7. European Cellars
European Cellars imports wines from family-owned properties practicing responsible viticulture. Its roots in France and Spain have expanded into other origins. Producers should assess how their wines express place and whether they add a distinct regional or stylistic contribution to the existing selection.
8. De Maison Selections
De Maison Selections is a national importer with a strong commitment to artisanal properties, regional heritage, and producer independence. Its business distinguishes national importing from direct distribution through De Maison East. Wineries should establish which relationship they are seeking before presenting their portfolio.
9. Polaner Selections
Polaner Selections combines established reference-point producers with smaller wineries, indigenous varieties, and less familiar regions. Its selection includes traditional producers and growers using organic or biodynamic practices. A compelling proposal should explain both the wine’s individuality and its value at the intended selling price.
10. Martine’s Wines
Martine’s Wines operates as an importer and wholesaler, with producer profiles and current wine information on its website. Its portfolio includes wines from established French regions and distinctive estates such as Domaine des Ardoisières. Suppliers should study the relevant regional selection before proposing additional representation. Importer & Wholesaler since 1979
Natural Wine and Small-Production Specialists
11. Jenny & François Selections
Jenny & François Selections focuses on natural wines from small growers. Its philosophy considers both vineyard practices and cellar methods. Producers researching the company should prepare a transparent account of farming, fermentation, additions, and production, alongside the practical information needed to evaluate a U.S. launch.
12. Zev Rovine Selections
Zev Rovine Selections works with growers who farm organically or biodynamically and favor minimal intervention in the cellar. Its producer list spans numerous countries. Wineries should assess philosophical fit and regional overlap, rather than assume a natural-wine identity alone creates an opening in the portfolio.
13. Selection Massale
Selection Massale imports natural wines from small wineries, emphasizing precision and drinkability. Its stated approach favors naturally fermented wines and growers working largely organically or biodynamically. Producers should explain how their practices translate into the wine’s character and consistency.
14. José Pastor Selections
José Pastor Selections champions small growers and traditionally made wines, with deep Spanish roots and a portfolio extending to other origins. Its selection includes regional grapes and distinctive vineyard environments. Wineries should explain what makes their wines an authentic expression of their particular place.
15. SelectioNaturel
SelectioNaturel specializes in Italian wines made in small quantities using natural and traditional methods. Its narrow focus makes regional and philosophical alignment especially important. Italian producers should study the represented growers and explain what their wines contribute beyond an appealing production story.
16. Vom Boden
Vom Boden focuses on small estates and growers whose work or locations sit outside the obvious mainstream. Its website includes current material on German wine. Producers considering the company should research its selection carefully and explain the vineyard, regional, and stylistic reasons their wines belong in that conversation.
17. Schatzi Wines
Schatzi Wines emphasizes the connection between growers and wine drinkers, with authenticity, sustainability, and terroir central to its approach. Its portfolio is built around producer relationships. Wineries should prepare clear information about their farming, wines, and expectations for a long-term importing partnership.
18. Olmstead Wine Co.
Olmstead Wine Co. is a Massachusetts distributor explicitly focused on natural wine. It provides a regional prospect for producers and importers whose wines fit that category. Suppliers should examine the portfolio and establish the current route for introducing new wines to the team.
19. Walden Selections
Walden Selections is a Washington State importer and distributor of wine and other beverages. It also appears in SelectioNaturel’s distribution network. Producers researching Washington should review the existing selection and discuss the specific importing or wholesale services required.
20. Nomadic Distribution
Nomadic Distribution presents itself as an importer and distributor of organic and natural wines. Its website includes producer information and a natural-wine shop. Suppliers should begin by reviewing the current producer list and confirming the relevant markets, portfolio needs, and submission process.
Regional and Country Specialists
21. The Piedmont Guy
The Piedmont Guy is a U.S.-based importer specializing in family-owned wineries from Piedmont. Its focused portfolio makes it particularly relevant to producers from that region. A pitch should explain the winery’s local identity, varieties, and position alongside the estates already represented.
22. Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits
Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits imports small-production Italian wines and operates distribution activities. Its stated preferences include clarity, freshness, indigenous varieties, and transparent winemaking. Producers should connect those characteristics with pricing and an account proposition that a sales team can readily explain.
23. Dalla Terra Italian Wine & Spirits
Dalla Terra describes its business as a national agent and direct importer for a select group of artisan, family-owned Italian wineries and spirits producers. Italian suppliers should understand its direct-import model and assess the existing regional portfolio before approaching the company.
24. Indigenous Selections
Indigenous Selections represents a curated group of Italian wineries selected for authenticity and regional character. Its portfolio covers origins including Piedmont, Tuscany, Veneto, Campania, Sicily, and Friuli. Producers should show how their wines offer a distinctive expression within the relevant region and price segment.
25. Porto Vino
Porto Vino maintains a French and Italian portfolio that includes producers from regions such as the Loire, Burgundy, Piedmont, and Sicily. Its website provides a detailed producer list. Suppliers should examine that regional coverage and explain where their wines add a meaningful point of difference.
26. North Berkeley Imports
North Berkeley Imports sources wines from France and Italy, combining importing with selected direct-market portfolios and distribution partners. Its offer reaches restaurants, wine shops, and collectors. Producers should distinguish the national portfolio opportunity from the company’s specific wholesale-market activities.
27. Michael Corso Selections
Michael Corso Selections is a specialist importer with a strong French wine focus. Its portfolio includes regions such as Alsace, Burgundy, the Loire, and the Rhône. Producers should present their regional credentials alongside a clear explanation of value and likely U.S. positioning.
28. Charles Neal Selections
Charles Neal Selections is a San Francisco-based importer and distributor with French wines and a substantial spirits selection. Its specialist approach makes it relevant to producers with a clear regional identity. Suppliers should explain the wine’s quality and commercial relevance without relying on small production as the sole selling point.
29. Brazos Wine Imports
Brazos Wine Imports focuses on artisan wines from Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay. Its stated interests include estate-grown, small-production wines that express specific places. South American producers should prepare detailed vineyard information and explain how the wines differ from more familiar market offerings.
30. Little Peacock Imports
Little Peacock Imports emphasizes a curated selection of family wineries, with producer listings covering Australia, France, Italy, and New Zealand. Its positioning combines discovery with commercial performance. Suppliers should explain why the wine is distinctive and how it can earn repeat purchases.
Curated Importers With Broader Portfolios
31. Grand Cru Selections
Grand Cru Selections is a New York-based importer and distributor with a strong fine-wine portfolio. Its producer information covers Champagne, Burgundy, and other regions. Wineries should research the existing estates closely and present a precise case for stylistic, regional, and commercial fit.
32. Coeur Wine Co.
Coeur Wine Co. emphasizes long-term producer relationships and wines it considers honest and authentic. Its website provides producer information and distribution partners. Suppliers should focus their introduction on the wine’s quality, its intended customer, and the practical foundations of a lasting relationship.
33. Communal Brands
Communal Brands combines production, importing, and distribution, with an emphasis on environmentally conscious wines and contemporary presentation. Its offer includes alternative formats such as boxed wine. Wineries should consider how product format, quality, and customer occasion work together within this business model.
34. Vine Connections
Vine Connections imports and distributes wines from family producers in origins including Argentina, Chile, Italy, France, and California. Its website provides trade tools such as technical sheets and shelf talkers. Producers should prepare a similarly complete set of materials when seeking representation. Global Wine, Sake & Spirits Importer
35. Massanois
Massanois is a national importer with direct distribution in selected markets. Its portfolio emphasizes quality-driven, family-owned wineries and distilleries. Suppliers should determine whether they need importing, direct wholesale distribution, or both, then tailor the proposal to the appropriate operation.
36. Banville Wine Merchants
Banville Wine Merchants combines national importing with wholesale operations in selected U.S. markets. Its approach centers on a selective, quality-focused portfolio. Producers should distinguish the national import opportunity from local distribution and identify the specific customer and price tier their wines would serve.
37. Regal Wine Imports
Regal Wine Imports maintains importing and distribution activities across wine and other beverage categories. Its website includes producer portfolios, trade information, and recent company content. Wineries should examine the relevant portfolio and market operation before proposing a new regional or stylistic addition.
38. Artisans & Vines
Artisans & Vines sources wines from Europe and several New World origins, emphasizing terroir and value. Its business includes importing, marketing, and distribution relationships. Suppliers should clarify the proposed territory and responsibilities, then connect their wine’s identity with a realistic market-development plan.
39. Wine Traditions
Wine Traditions seeks independent growers whose wines express their vineyards and offer accessible value. It operates as a national imp

Artisanal Spirits Importers in the USA: A Gateway to Craftsmanship and Authenticity
Photo for: Artisanal Spirits Importers in the USA: A Gateway to Craftsmanship and Authenticity
16/10/2024 Boutique importers of artisanal spirits have a special place in the US market.
In the U.S. spirits market, where mass-produced brands dominate, boutique importers play a vital role in bringing unique, high-quality, and artisanal products to discerning consumers. These importers, often specializing in small-batch, independently produced spirits, are key to promoting craftsmanship, authenticity, and diversity within the industry. While global brands may occupy much of the shelf space, boutique importers offer a curated selection of spirits that reflect the artistry and tradition of their producers, helping to drive consumer interest in the growing artisanal spirits segment.
The Role of Artisanal Spirits Importers
Artisanal spirits importers serve as the bridge between small distilleries worldwide and the U.S. market. They focus on bringing in spirits that offer more than just high quality—products with unique stories, authentic production methods, and distinctive flavors. By doing so, they cater to a growing consumer base that values authenticity and craftsmanship over mass production.
For instance, companies like Shand Import and Double Eagle Imports take pride in selecting spirits that embody tradition and innovation. Shand Import offers a portfolio featuring craft Tequilas, Mezcals, and rare Scotch whiskies, showcasing their commitment to quality and the spirit of discovery. Meanwhile, Double Eagle Imports focuses specifically on Agave spirits, utilizing their deep industry knowledge to promote the craftsmanship of independent Mexican distilleries. They combine efficient route-to-market strategies with educational marketing campaigns that emphasize storytelling and consumer engagement, helping these artisanal brands thrive in the competitive U.S. marketplace.
Source: Shand Import LLC
Building Brands One Bottle at a Time
What sets boutique importers apart is their hands-on approach to brand building. Unlike larger importers, who often deal with high volumes and established names, artisanal importers work closely with small producers to develop their brands from the ground up. Companies like Massanois and PKGD Group exemplify this. Massanois not only imports but also distributes fine wines and spirits, supporting small family-owned distilleries from across the globe, from Armenia to Argentina. They provide these producers with the necessary tools to succeed by fostering relationships with top-tier restaurants and retailers and tailoring their messaging to resonate with U.S. consumers.
PKGD Group goes a step further by offering integrated services that encompass brand development, management, and spirits importing. They work with a curated selection of spirits, offering transparency and expertise in helping producers establish a presence in the market. Their focus on premium spirits at various stages of brand growth highlights their commitment to nurturing talent and ensuring the success of the brands they represent.
Source: Artisanal Spirits Company
The Value of Authenticity and Storytelling
In today’s market, consumers increasingly seek brands that offer more than just a product—they want a connection to the people, places, and processes behind the spirits they consume. Boutique importers recognize this and often base their marketing strategies on storytelling, highlighting the history, tradition, and innovation behind each brand.
Barbera Imports and ARQ Spirits, for example, are dedicated to helping luxury and artisanal producers navigate the complex U.S. market by crafting personalized strategies tailored to each brand. Barbera Imports emphasizes a seamless approach to guiding brands through the regulatory and logistical challenges of the three-tier system, while ARQ Spirits provides specialized sales and channel development services. Both companies ensure that each brand's unique story is front and center, helping to build a lasting connection between the producer and the consumer.

Encouraging Consumer Exploration and Craft Spirits Growth
A significant part of the appeal of artisanal spirits lies in their versatility and the potential for experimentation. Importers like Double Eagle Imports focus on encouraging consumers to explore new flavors and approaches to craft mixology, while also promoting the pairing of high-quality sipping tequilas with food. This emphasis on experimentation helps to cultivate a more engaged and adventurous consumer base, driving the growth of the craft spirits segment in the U.S. market.
As consumers become more educated about craft spirits, the demand for authentic, high-quality products continues to rise. Boutique importers play a crucial role in satisfying this demand by sourcing innovative and rare spirits that challenge the status quo. Their expertise in identifying and promoting emerging trends allows them to stay ahead of market shifts and provide their customers with a fresh and exciting selection of spirits.
Boutique Importers as Industry Gatekeepers
While boutique importers might represent a small fraction of the overall U.S. spirits market, their impact is significant. By focusing on quality over quantity and nurturing relationships with independent producers, these importers act as gatekeepers for authenticity and craftsmanship. They ensure that only the finest and most unique spirits reach the market, offering consumers a diverse array of products that they might otherwise never encounter.
Moreover, these importers are instrumental in helping small distilleries navigate the often challenging U.S. regulatory landscape. Importers like Shand Import and Barbera Imports specialize in the intricacies of the three-tier system, working to ensure that artisanal brands are able to find their footing in a market dominated by established players. Through their efforts, boutique importers help to level the playing field and provide a platform for small producers to compete on quality and uniqueness.
In the final analysis, artisanal spirits importers are the unsung heroes of the craft spirits movement. By championing craftsmanship, authenticity, and the stories behind each bottle, they are helping to shape the future of the U.S. spirits market. Their dedication to sourcing and promoting small-batch, independent producers not only benefits consumers seeking unique, high-quality products but also supports the growth and sustainability of the global craft spirits industry.
As the demand for artisanal spirits continues to grow, the importance of these boutique importers will only increase. They play a crucial role in introducing consumers to new flavors, traditions, and innovations, ensuring that the craft spirits movement remains vibrant and dynamic for years to come.
Take a look at some of the leading boutique importers of artisanal spirits in the USA.
1. Shand Imports
Shand Imports is a boutique company based in Los Angeles, California, specializing in the import of premium craft spirits from around the globe. With a portfolio built on quality, authenticity, and craftsmanship—from the finest tequilas and mezcals of Mexico to rare single malt and blended Scotch whiskies, Shand Imports is dedicated to curating an unparalleled selection of world-class spirits for the U.S. market.
Image Credits: Shand Imports
2. Massanois
Massanois is a New York-based importer and distributor that champions family-owned wineries and distilleries from across the globe. With a national reach extending to 45 U.S. states, their portfolio spans renowned wine and spirit-producing regions including Argentina, France, Italy, and Japan. Operating both as an importer and distributor, Massanois focuses on connecting top-tier producers with key restaurants, retailers, and distributors.
Image Credits: Massanois
3. Double Eagle Imports
Established in 2006, Double Eagle Imports Ltd has carved out a niche as a leading importer and marketer of craft spirits defined by their high quality, innovative branding, and exceptional value. Specializing in super-premium tequilas from independent distilleries, Double Eagle’s mission is to tell the story behind each Agave spirit they represent. Through focused marketing on craftsmanship and consumer education, they work to elevate the appreciation of craft spirits in the U.S..
